seoTitle: Turn an Excel Spreadsheet Into a Smartsheet
metaDescription: Import an Excel file into Smartsheet using the native Import Excel tool, map your columns, and activate Gantt, Card, and Calendar views instantly.
intro: Migrating from static Excel spreadsheets to a dynamic Smartsheet workspace is mostly a matter of cleaning up your file and running the import wizard. This guide covers preparing your Excel data, mapping columns during import, and activating interactive views once your data lands in Smartsheet.

steps.heading: Clean up your Excel file first
steps.body: Establish a clean header row and remove merged cells to ensure a flawless import.

steps.heading: Open the Import Excel tool
steps.body: Navigate to the Smartsheet Solution Center and select the native Import Excel function.

steps.heading: Upload and configure your file
steps.body: Upload your .xlsx or .xls file and use the configuration step to designate your primary task columns.

steps.heading: Map your column types
steps.body: Assign fields like Dropdown lists, Text/Number, Dates, and Contact Lists inside the import preview.

steps.heading: Activate interactive views
steps.body: Turn on Gantt Charts, Card Views, or Calendar Views instantly from your newly imported data.

faq.question: Why should I clean up my Excel file before importing?
faq.answer: Establishing a clean header row and removing merged cells helps ensure the import maps correctly without errors.

faq.question: What Excel formats can I import?
faq.answer: Smartsheet's Import Excel tool accepts both .xlsx and .xls file formats.

faq.question: Can I set column types like dropdowns during import?
faq.answer: Yes, the import preview lets you map fields to Dropdown lists, Text/Number, Dates, and Contact List columns.

faq.question: Do I get Gantt charts automatically after importing?
faq.answer: Once imported, you can activate Gantt Charts, Card Views, or Calendar Views instantly from the same data.
